summary: Saddle Blanket Mountain tower in the Willamette National Forest: 1922 tree lookout, 1927 steel tower, abandoned 1967; NHLR-registered 1991.

facts.design: Aermotor LX-24 steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: Abandoned as a lookout in 1967; the steel tower was still in place at a July 2013 visit. No later condition report was found.

access.note: Reached on foot by Saddleblanket Trail 3487 from the end of Forest Road 144. The tower is not open as a lookout, and climbing is discouraged.

visit.trail_note: Trail 3487 begins on the left side of the end of Forest Road 144. A 2013 visitor hiked a brushy 1.5-mile trail to the lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1922 is the crow's nest in a tree; the steel tower is dated 1927 by the Register and firelookout.com. A 1927 Eugene Guard item says the 60-foot tower was erected last year, and a 1925 Morning Register item says its foundations were already in, so the year the tower went up is 1926 or 1927 depending on the source.

notes_for_editor: Current condition unknown: the latest source read is Cheryl Hill's July 2013 visit, which found the steel tower in place; no later report of the tower's condition or of the 1969 sale outcome was found. Do not treat it as standing today without a recent check. Record fixes: built 1922 is the crow's nest (proposed 1927); height_m 9.1 is 30 feet, the tree lookout (proposed 21.3 m for the 70-foot tower). Unresolved disagreements, not settled by the sources: tower height 60 feet (1926-27 Eugene paper) against 70 feet (Register, 1953 survey station, 1969 notices, Cheryl Hill); tower date 1926 (1927 newspaper 'last year') against 1927 (Register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill); elevation 4,940 ft (Register) against 4,969 ft (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill, Forest Service); abandonment 1967 (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill) against the 1969 notices, which say it 'no longer will be manned' in fire season. The Register's 'Built' field is not given; the 1927 date is taken from its description. Access: the Forest Service trail page gives the route as 1.1 miles along Road 142 to Road 144, then 0.8 mile to the end of Road 144, where the trail begins; the 1969 newspaper described a road stopping several hundred yards short, which may be a different route. No photos added.
